title: Pantry Organization
subtitle: First in, first out — and the two date words that are not the same.
objectives: Decide where each kind of food is stored
Explain why dry goods go into sealed containers

cards.title: A pantry is a system with a direction
cards.text: Food goes in at the back and comes out at the front. Get that one habit and almost nothing expires unopened.

cards.title: First in, first out
cards.text: FIFO. Two letters of it do all the work.
points: **New stock goes behind** the old.
**Nearest expiry sits in front.**
**You reach for the front** without thinking.
**Shops run on this.** So should a cupboard.

cards.title: You decide where it goes
cards.text: Four items. Pick a place and see what would actually happen.

question.text: Two identical tins, one expiring sooner. Which goes in front?
question.explain: FIFO. You will reach for the front one.

cards.title: Four places, four reasons
cards.text: The reason is always moisture, temperature or light.
points: **Fridge, at or under 4°C** — anything perishable.
**Freezer at -18°C** — long storage; growth stopped.
**Cool dark cupboard** — oil, rice, flour. Light turns oil rancid.
**Open shelf** — tins and jars only.

question.text: Why does cooking oil go in a dark cupboard?
question.explain: Light and heat both break it down.

cards.title: Two different words that people treat as one
cards.text: Only one of them is about safety.
points: **Use by** — a safety date. Do not eat it after.
**Best before** — a quality date. It is legal to eat.
**Opened changes everything.** The date on the tin assumed it was shut.
**Write the opening date** on the container.

cards.title: A pantry is a chest you have to sort
cards.text: Same problem, same solution, every game you have played.
points: **Stacks of the same item together.**
**Oldest used first** so nothing decays in storage.
**Labels, because you will not remember.**
**A full chest you cannot read** is the same as an empty one.

cards.title: A mission pantry is the extreme version
cards.text: Nothing can spoil, nothing can be restocked, and mass costs money.
points: **Freeze-dried**, so water is removed and growth cannot start.
**Water is added back** on board.
**Every item is dated and tracked.**
**A pantry with no shop** is a pantry run properly.

cards.title: Sealed containers, labelled
cards.text: The same instinct that keeps a screw from being lost.
points: **Opened rice in a bag** gets weevils and damp.
**Opened rice in a sealed jar** keeps for months.
**Label it with the date opened.**
**Future you is a stranger.** Write it down.

cards.title: What to remember
points: FIFO: new stock behind, nearest expiry in front.
Fridge 4°C, freezer -18°C, oil and rice cool and dark.
Use by is safety; best before is quality.
Opened dry goods go into something that seals, with the date on it.

quiz.explain: So you reach for the oldest.

quiz.text: A fridge should run at or below…
quiz.explain: Low enough to slow growth to almost nothing.
quiz.objective: Decide where each kind of food is stored

quiz.text: A freezer should run at about…
quiz.objective: Decide where each kind of food is stored

quiz.text: Why does rice go in a sealed container once opened?
options: It expires faster in air only
quiz.explain: A folded-over bag is not a seal.
quiz.objective: Explain why dry goods go into sealed containers

quiz.explain: Do not eat it after that.
Quality drops; it is still legal to eat.

quiz.text: A date on a tin still applies once the tin is open.
quiz.explain: The date assumed it was sealed. Write the opening date on it.
Nothing can drip onto other food.
quiz.objective: Decide where each kind of food is stored

quiz.text: Why is cooking oil kept out of the light?
quiz.explain: Light and heat break it down.
quiz.objective: Decide where each kind of food is stored

options: water is removed, so growth cannot start
quiz.explain: No water, no growth. Water is added back on board.
quiz.objective: Explain why dry goods go into sealed containers

quiz.text: The real reason to label an opened container is that…
options: you will not remember when you opened it
quiz.objective: Explain why dry goods go into sealed containers

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 4 TLE. One habit carries the week: new stock behind, nearest expiry in front. The interactive makes him decide where four items go, and each wrong placement is answered with what would happen to the food, including the cooked-rice case from week 3 so the two weeks reinforce. The use-by against best-before distinction is given carefully because it is both commonly confused and genuinely about safety in one direction only, and because it is the knowledge that stops a household throwing away edible food. The space lens is the honest extreme: a pantry with no shop, every item dated and tracked.
discussion: Ask which tin goes in front and why.
Ask the difference between use by and best before.
Ask what the date on a tin assumes.
Ask why oil is kept in the dark.
extension: Have him reorganise one shelf by FIFO and label anything opened.
Have him check the fridge and freezer temperatures against the targets.
misconceptions: "Use by and best before mean the same." Only one is about safety.
"The printed date still applies once it is open." It assumed a seal.
"Newest to the front looks tidier." It is how food expires unopened.
